subject: research/ambient-rechime
professional: a senior human-factors engineer for auditory alerts and wearable notifications (auditory-warning practice in the Patterson/Edworthy tradition, ISO 7731 masked-threshold audibility, IEC 60601-1-8 alarm repetition); first checks: where P(tone detected) and the look/reaction rates come from, whether detections across repeats are treated as independent, how annoyance grows with repeats, and whether the closed form matches the stated stochastic model

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with my own script that does not import the subject (scratchpad rechime/indep.py, python3.13 -I): a forward recursion over a two-state (unalerted / alerted, not yet looked) process between tone times, parameters re-typed from the README Method section, a different formulation from sim.py's closed-form sum. It reproduces every number in results.txt sections 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 to 4 decimals: fixed n=0..4 0.2257/0.3680/0.3712/0.3648/0.3594; best of 0..1/0..2/0..4 0.3866/0.4058/0.4090; best-n shares by urgency identical; gains 0.0002/0.0371/0.0618; all eight gap x cancel gains; all five mask rows. An event-by-event pure-Python Monte Carlo (200,000 draws, competing exponentials, my own code) for high urgency, 6 words, noise 0.5, others 1, eyes free, n=3 gives 1.6585 vs closed form 1.6598. Hand calcs: plain glance high/6 words/free = 2(1-e^-0.6)-0.08 = 0.822377 and one tone at no noise = 2(1-e^-3.6)-0.08-0.04 = 1.825353, both equal to utility() to 1e-15. The code computes exactly the model it states; the model's inputs are invented (see domain).
evidence.completeness: Claims checked: 9 tests (9 pass, as README says); run.py reproduces results.txt byte-identically (diff empty, 0.56 s, 'a few seconds'); figure.py regenerates chime_mask.svg with no git diff; research/README.md:442 entry present; limitations and next steps listed. Live page https://marisstella.app/research/ambient-rechime/ not reachable (proxy 403), not counted against it. Everything the README says was done was done.
evidence.verification: `cd research/ambient-rechime && PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 9 passed in 0.11 s. Tests cover the n=0 analytic case, monotone P(seen) in tones, a one-tone analytic case, expected-tones bounds, deadline truncation, closed form vs the in-repo Monte Carlo, and option-set monotonicity. Five mutants via quality_mutate.py: caught 2 (p_unseen geometric exponent j -> j+1 at sim.py:54; tone cost loses the others-talking multiplier at sim.py:70); survived 3 (best_n tie-break -n -> n at sim.py:100; high-urgency weight 2.0 -> 1.5 at sim.py:9; react_busy_factor 0.3 -> 1.0 at sim.py:26). No test pins any results.txt number, so a changed parameter or class definition shifts every headline silently. The Monte Carlo check shares the author's model assumptions, so it checks algebra, not the model.
evidence.craft: Read sim.py (114 lines), run.py, figure.py, test_sim.py. Small, readable, closed form plus vectorised MC, results written by code and the figure parsed from results.txt. Defects: in simulate the hit mask '& (s < t_look)' (sim.py:82) is dead, t_look is still all-inf there and is assigned only at sim.py:87, so the line reads as if it gates tones on the look when it does not (results happen to be right because only the first noticed tone matters); run.py:45 labels section 6 'tones n=1' while it computes the best of 0 and 1; with_ is a one-line alias of dataclasses.replace.
evidence.claims: Backed: every number in README Results 1-6 and the headline by results.txt (recomputed independently); 'two or three 18%' (0.08+0.10); masking deltas 0.039/0.062/0.056/0.036; stylised disclosure, AI-assistance note, 'orderings follow from the model, sizes are not estimates', independence and flat-annoyance limitations stated. Weak: README:63 'cancelling ... worth up to 0.006' (the gain differences are 0.0042/0.0067/0.0064/0.0060 and my direct value of cancelling, best of 0..4 with minus without, is 0.0066, so it rounds down); README:66 'fade when they are nearly always missed' at chime_mask 1.0, where the noise grid makes P(miss) 0, 0.5 or 1 across contexts, so the average tone is missed half the time; README:26 Horvitz cited 'not re-read here'. Minor, not a wrong headline.
evidence.fitness: A researcher on wearable notification timing could take the closed form (Poisson look process with a rate step after the first detected tone) as a starting template, but nothing here is a result they can cite: every rate and cost is a round number with no source and only gap and masking are swept. Nearest prior work: probability summation over repeated presentations in signal detection (Green and Swets 1966), auditory-warning burst repetition guidance (Patterson 1982, CAA Paper 82017; IEC 60601-1-8 alarm repetition), and attention-sensitive notification decision models (Horvitz, Kadie, Paek and Hovel 2003, CACM 'Models of attention in computing and communication'; Pielot et al. 2014, MobileHCI, in-situ notification response times) (citations from memory, not re-read in this audit). The finding that a second tone helps most at moderate miss rates and short deadlines is 1-(1-p)^n with a cost term, not new. The README does not claim novelty, so novelty is not overstated, but it falls well short of research/CLAUDE.md's PhD-level, sourced-parameter bar (it is on the legacy list, research/_shared/legacy_projects.txt:82, so programme_check does not hold it).
evidence.domain: Against auditory-alert practice: tone detection is a flat 1 - 0.5 x noise rather than a masked-threshold (ISO 7731) or signal-to-noise model; detections across repeats are independent (stated as a limitation, and it biases the headline gain upward); annoyance is flat per tone with no growth (stated); look and reaction rates (0.1/s, +0.5/s) are invented rather than taken from published notification response-time data, contrary to research/CLAUDE.md 'Run the numbers; don't stylise them'; the glance cost is charged whether or not the wearer looks by the deadline (inherited from ambient-urgency; constant across n so it does not move best_n). A senior practitioner would not sign off on the sizes, and the README itself says the sizes are not estimates.

verdict: Small, honest, exactly reproducible stylised model. Every number in results.txt and the README headline (0.387 -> 0.409 mean utility per message) was recomputed with an independent forward recursion and an independent event-level Monte Carlo and matches to 4 decimals; run.py reproduces results.txt byte-identically and the 9 tests pass. It misses the bar on verification (3 of 5 seeded mutants survive; no test pins a result) and is far from the research bar on fitness and domain: all driving parameters are invented round figures, detections are independent, and the trade-off it shows is textbook probability summation with a cost term, with no prior work on auditory warnings or notification response times cited. Novelty is not claimed, so not overstated.
